context.objective: Document how we carry out Capital Call & Distribution Event Execution, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: To begin with, we open the event and assign responsibility. That is done by: Assigned CAP Activity Team or Fund Team preparer. What we do: classify the event as a call, distribution, or net event; record the business driver, affected entity, requested amount, urgency, and expected cash dates; assign the preparing team and second reviewer before calculations begin; identify related subprocesses required, including , , , , or . The check on it: responsible team and reviewer are explicit; no event proceeds with ambiguous ownership. Next, we establish the event calendar. That is done by: Event preparer. What we do: determine the contractual notice period and whether it uses business or calendar days; set internal preparation, review, client-approval, posting, notice-release, due/payment, and post-event dates; check bank holidays and payment cut-offs for any cash-out event; allow time for external tax coordination and Investor Services campaign preparation where applicable. The check on it: reviewer confirms the contractual due-date calculation and critical operational dates.
What typically prompts the preparer to open a capital call or distribution event?

After that, we assemble the event data pack. That is done by: Event preparer. What we do: collect call inputs: investment funding, management fees, expense projections, and LOC principal/interest as applicable; collect distribution inputs: expected/received proceeds, deal character, waterfall support, tax income, and withholding as applicable; obtain the current investor/partner population and all known onboarding, transfer, joiner, leaver, waiver, offset, or special-allocation information; obtain the prior locked event file, notices, power report, TB, and partner-capital support; mark every input as final, estimated, or pending. The check on it: reviewer can trace each material input to a provider or source document. Then, we roll forward the allocation engine and establish continuity. That is done by: Event preparer. What we do: copy the final prior event model to create the new event file; update the event dates, narrative, and entity information; pull beginning balances from the correct system report and as-of date; tie beginning contributions, distributions, proceeds, partner capital, and unfunded balances to the prior deliverable; record and explain any difference before continuing. The check on it: zero unexplained difference to the prior deliverable.
When the beginning balances do not tie to the prior deliverable, what happens before the event can continue?

Once that is done, we freeze the rules of the run. That is done by: Event preparer with second reviewer and client input. What we do: document whether allocations use unfunded commitment, total commitment, LP-only percentage, deal-level, or another governing basis; document new-investment versus follow-on treatment; record offsets, credits, exclusions, special allocations, and carry treatment; for a distribution, link the approved waterfall/tax methodology; obtain written client confirmation for any changed or ambiguous treatment. The check on it: second reviewer confirms consistency with governing documents; client confirms changed or ambiguous rules. Following that, we complete the population gate. That is done by: Event preparer; second reviewer performs independent check. What we do: list every investor or partner expected in the event; confirm new investors are effective and portal-ready; confirm subsequent-close treatment where applicable; remove departing investors from future capital calls only when the governing documents or client direction require it; apply waiver funding only to eligible members and document any departure-related restructuring; apply approved transfers, reallocations, offsets, and exclusions; compare the population to the prior event and explain every change. The check on it: independent reviewer confirms every addition, removal, and special treatment.
How does the preparer decide the event data pack is ready for calculations when inputs are marked estimated or pending?

Following that, we run the allocation calculations. That is done by: Event preparer. What we do: enter the approved event amounts and apply the documented allocation basis; calculate investor/partner-level components; for distributions, incorporate the approved waterfall, tax distribution, and withholding outputs; for net events, retain separate call and distribution components before calculating the net amount; populate the summary allocation tab used by the notice merge; check that the results are reasonable compared with the total event amounts and prior patterns. The check on it: component totals and investor totals equal the approved fund- level event amount, subject only to documented rounding. Following that, we reconcile the event. That is done by: Event preparer; second reviewer verifies. What we do: reconcile allocation outputs to partner capital and prior balances; reconcile remaining GP unfunded to the fund; reconcile the workbook to the TB and other accounting support; document known client-specific differences and their governing treatment; confirm the allocation summary agrees to all detailed tabs. The check on it: zero unexplained difference across totals, beginning balances, unfunded, and matches to the trial balance (TB).
What usually prompts the team to open a capital call or distribution event?

topics.answer: Capital Call & Distribution Event Execution
The event is opened as the first described work, but the initiating event or condition that causes the team to open it is not established.

The observable finished condition for the event, including whether posting, notice release, payment, or post-event work must be complete, is not established; these are calendar dates only in the account.
The role accountable for the overall result is not established; the account identifies preparers and a second reviewer but does not say who owns the result.

The assigned CAP Activity Team or Fund Team preparer opens and classifies the event as a call, distribution or net event; records the business driver, affected entity, requested amount, urgency and expected cash dates; assigns the preparing team and second reviewer before calculations; and identifies required related subprocesses.
After event opening, the event preparer establishes an event calendar: determines the contractual notice period and whether it uses business or calendar days, then sets internal preparation, review, client-approval, posting, notice-release, due/payment, and post-event dates. For a cash-out event, the preparer checks bank holidays and payment cut-offs; where applicable, time is allowed for external tax coordination and Investor Services campaign preparation.
After calendar setup, the event preparer assembles a data pack: call inputs include investment funding, management fees, expense projections and applicable LOC principal and interest; distribution inputs include expected or received proceeds, deal character, waterfall support, tax income and applicable withholding.
The event preparer obtains the current investor/partner population and known onboarding, transfer, joiner, leaver, waiver, offset and special-allocation information, as well as the prior locked event file, notices, power report, TB and partner-capital support. Each input is marked final, estimated or pending.
The event preparer copies the final prior event model to create the new file, updates dates, narrative and entity information, and pulls beginning balances from the correct system report and as-of date. The preparer ties beginning contributions, distributions, proceeds, partner capital and unfunded balances to the prior deliverable and records and explains differences before continuing.
After continuity, the event preparer freezes the run rules with second-reviewer and client input: documents the allocation basis and new-investment versus follow-on treatment, records offsets, credits, exclusions, special allocations and carry treatment, and links approved waterfall and tax methodology for distributions. Written client confirmation is obtained for changed or ambiguous treatment.
The preparer then lists expected investors or partners, confirms new investors are effective and portal-ready and confirms applicable subsequent-close treatment. Departing investors are removed from future calls only when governing documents or client direction require it; waiver funding is applied only to eligible members and departure-related restructuring is documented.
At the population gate, the preparer applies approved transfers, reallocations, offsets and exclusions, compares the population with the prior event and explains every change. A second reviewer independently confirms every addition, removal and special treatment.
Following the population gate, the preparer enters approved event amounts, applies the documented basis and calculates investor/partner-level components. For distributions the preparer incorporates approved waterfall, tax distribution and withholding outputs; for net events separate call and distribution components are retained before calculating the net.
The preparer populates the summary allocation tab used by the notice merge and checks results for reasonableness against event totals and prior patterns. The preparer then reconciles outputs to partner capital and prior balances, remaining GP unfunded to the fund, the workbook to TB and accounting support, and the summary to detailed tabs; client-specific differences and governing treatment are documented. The second reviewer verifies.
The readiness decision for calculation when data-pack inputs are estimated or pending has not been explained.

At event opening, the check is that the responsible team and reviewer are explicit; no event proceeds with ambiguous ownership. The second reviewer confirms the contractual due-date calculation and critical operational dates on the event calendar.
The account names a client-approval date but does not establish who approves, what is reviewed, whether approval blocks release, or what happens if it is delayed or rejected.
For the data pack, the reviewer must be able to trace each material input to a provider or source document.
Continuity requires zero unexplained difference to the prior deliverable; the event preparer records and explains differences before continuing.
The second reviewer confirms run rules against governing documents, and the client confirms changed or ambiguous treatment in writing. The second reviewer independently checks every population addition, removal and special treatment.
Allocation component and investor totals must equal the approved fund-level event amount subject only to documented rounding. Reconciliation requires zero unexplained differences across totals, beginning balances, unfunded and TB matches.
The handling of unexplained reconciliation differences and the evidence retained for the review are not yet described.

For cash-out events, the preparer checks bank holidays and payment cut-offs. The calendar also allows time for external tax coordination and Investor Services campaign preparation where applicable.
The circumstances requiring external tax coordination or Investor Services campaign preparation are unspecified.
Distribution events incorporate approved waterfall, tax distribution and withholding outputs; net events retain separate call and distribution components before calculating the net. The account also calls for documenting known client-specific reconciliation differences and their governing treatment, but does not identify individual differences.

The event calendar sets internal preparation, review, client-approval, posting, notice-release, due/payment and post-event dates.
The event calendar's format, storage location and custodian are not identified.
The event data pack includes the current investor/partner population, relevant changes and special allocations, prior locked event file, notices, power report, TB and partner-capital support. Inputs are labeled final, estimated or pending.
The final prior event model is copied to create the new event file for allocation-engine continuity.
The allocation workbook contains a summary allocation tab used by the notice merge and detailed tabs reconciled to that summary. Written client confirmation records changed or ambiguous treatment.

The described event categories are calls, distributions and net events; the preparer records the affected entity.
The full range and number of entities in scope remain unspecified; the account identifies fund-level event amounts.
The reported calculation works at investor or partner level and ties to an approved fund-level event amount; reconciliation includes remaining GP unfunded.

The event preparer determines the contractual notice period and whether it uses business or calendar days; the reviewer confirms the contractual due-date calculation and critical operational dates.
The source establishing the contractual notice period and the method for resolving any conflicting terms are not identified.
Before continuing from the allocation-engine roll-forward, differences against the prior deliverable must be recorded and explained, with zero unexplained difference.
The documented allocation basis may be unfunded commitment, total commitment, LP-only percentage, deal-level or another governing basis. New versus follow-on investment treatment and applicable offsets, credits, exclusions, special allocations and carry treatment are recorded.
Changed or ambiguous treatment requires written client confirmation; the second reviewer checks consistency with governing documents. Distribution calculations incorporate approved waterfall, tax distribution and withholding outputs, and rounding differences must be documented.
A departing investor is removed from future calls only when governing documents or client direction require it, and waiver funding is restricted to eligible members.

The event calendar allows time for external tax coordination and Investor Services campaign preparation where applicable.
The listed related subprocess names are blank; specific handoffs and readiness evidence for tax coordination and Investor Services are not described.

The event preparer creates the new event file by copying the final prior event model and pulls beginning balances from the correct system report and as-of date.
The system and report supplying beginning balances, workbook location and detailed allocation-engine implementation remain unidentified.
The preparer enters approved amounts into the allocation calculation and populates a summary tab for the notice merge; the workbook is reconciled to the TB and other accounting support.

steps.title: Open event and assign responsibility
steps.actor: Assigned CAP Activity Team or Fund Team preparer
steps.description: Classify the event as a call, distribution or net event; record its business driver, affected entity, requested amount, urgency and expected cash dates. Assign the preparing team and second reviewer before calculations and identify required related subprocesses. Ownership must be explicit before the event proceeds.

steps.title: Establish the event calendar
steps.description: Determine the contractual notice period and whether it uses business or calendar days. Set preparation, review, client-approval, posting, notice-release, due/payment and post-event dates. Check bank holidays and payment cut-offs for cash-out events, and allow time for tax coordination and Investor Services campaign preparation where applicable.

steps.title: Review event calendar dates
steps.description: Confirm the contractual due-date calculation and critical operational dates.

steps.title: Assemble the event data pack
steps.description: Collect applicable call and distribution inputs, the current investor and partner population, known population and allocation changes, and prior-event support. Mark each input final, estimated or pending; the reviewer must be able to trace each material input to a provider or source document.

steps.title: Roll forward and tie balances
steps.description: Copy the final prior event model, update event details and pull beginning balances from the correct system report and as-of date. Tie contributions, distributions, proceeds, partner capital and unfunded balances to the prior deliverable; record and explain differences before continuing.

steps.title: Freeze the run rules
steps.actor: Event preparer with second reviewer and client input
steps.description: Document the allocation basis, investment treatment, offsets, exclusions, special allocations and carry treatment. For distributions, link the approved waterfall and tax methodology. Obtain written client confirmation for changed or ambiguous treatment; the second reviewer confirms consistency with governing documents.

steps.title: Complete the population gate
steps.actor: Event preparer; second reviewer performs independent check
steps.description: List expected investors or partners, confirm applicable new-investor and subsequent-close treatment, and apply approved population changes and special treatments. Remove departing investors from future calls only when governing documents or client direction require it; apply waiver funding only to eligible members. Compare the population with the prior event and explain every change; the second reviewer independently confirms additions, removals and special treatment.

steps.title: Run allocation calculations
steps.description: Enter approved event amounts and apply the documented basis to calculate investor or partner components. Incorporate approved waterfall, tax distribution and withholding outputs for distributions; retain separate call and distribution components before calculating net amounts for net events. Populate the notice-merge summary and check results against event totals and prior patterns.

steps.title: Reconcile the event
steps.description: Reconcile allocations to partner capital and prior balances, remaining GP unfunded to the fund, and the workbook to the trial balance and other accounting support. Document known client-specific differences and their governing treatment, and confirm the summary agrees with detailed tabs.
